name: Prize crossword No 26,950

clue.text: American dance English society shunned

explanation.surface: A dance from America that polite English society refused to touch.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble's eleven are the England team that won the 1966 football World Cup; Jack and Bobby Charlton were both in it, so CHARLTON appears twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack Charlton played centre-half in England's winning side of 1966 alongside his brother.

clue.text: Religious leader creating new circle

taken as written

clue.text: The French prohibition operating in a Mediterranean country

explanation.definitionFit: Lebanon is a state on the eastern shore of the Mediterranean Sea, bordering Syria and Israel.

clue.text: Nothing stays still with energy in old play

explanation.definitionFit: Orestes is a tragedy by Euripides, written in ancient Athens about Agamemnon's son.

explanation.definitionFit: Alan Ball was the young midfielder in England's 1966 World Cup-winning side.

clue.text: Remove black stuff from vehicle sunk in bottom of river after reversing

explanation.definitionFit: George Cohen was the Fulham right-back who played in every England game of the 1966 World Cup.

clue.text: Orchestra in triumph

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fired' looks like it belongs with the cartridges, but it means dismissed. Gordon Banks was England's goalkeeper in 1966.

clue.text: Fighting unit to strike bellicose male, reservists brought in

explanation.definitionFit: A battalion is a large army formation of several companies, a unit of soldiers.

clue.text: Something required not so much, not half creating anger

clue.text: Monster insects (two of them) hard to catch

clue.text: Sort of barrier when children start school with hesitation

explanation.walkthrough: 'Chancellor' suggests a finance minister, but this is Thomas More, executed in 1535. Bobby Moore captained England to the 1966 World Cup.

clue.text: Short day, beginning to end
